false_statements.quote: Starch and cellulose both contain glucose units, so both function primarily as energy-storage polysaccharides.
false_statements.why: Cellulose does not function primarily for energy storage. Starch stores glucose for later energy use, while cellulose chains are organized to support plant cell walls. Sharing glucose monomers does not confer the same function.

object.verdict_reason: Keyed answer A is false; cellulose is structural, not energy-storage. Choice D is the factually correct answer and must be keyed instead. Content is otherwise accurate and within CED, so re-keying (not rejection) fixes it.
